newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends sharply higher on PV outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends sharply higher on PV outage.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Tuesday on a late rally triggered in part by news of a brief outage of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Palo Verde (PV) nuclear station due to a steam leak
PV's unit 1 scaled back production late Monday while investigating the problem. The unit in Wintersburg, Ariz., was in the process of returning from a refueling outage.
PV along with the California-Oregon Border (COB) are the designated delivery points of the electricity contracts,
The operator, Arizona Public Service Co (APS) said it expected the unit would startup within 24 hours after the steam leak was repaired.
Some participants downplayed the signficance of the shutdown of PV unit 1 because of its short duration.

Physical and futures power prices were buoyed earlier today by firmer natural gas prices, continued absence of Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) from the daily market, and an unplanned outage of a 720 MW coal-fired unit at the Four Corners generating facility in Arizona late Monday.
Four Corners' unit 1 was expected to be shut six days, said APS, which also operates the Four Corners' plant.
December COB futures settled up $1.68 at $24.49 a megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a low of $22.75.
January COB finished up $1.36 to $21.88. Deferred COB ended 70 cents to $1.36 higher.
December PV futures settled up $1.63 at $22.38 after traded between $21.35 and $22.75.
January PV finished at $19.67, up 92 cents. Outer PV months ended 75 cents to $1.85 higher.
After today's close in over-the-counter activity, December COB was discussed at $24.25-$25.25, and December PV $22.25-$22.75.
"As long as gas prices stay high, weather stays cold and BPA stays out of the market, prices will go higher," said a Houston trader.
NYMEX estimated 296 COB and 41 PV contracts were sold.
